newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle seen steady to up, feeders higher.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle seen steady to up, feeders higher.

text.p: CME live cattle futures were expected to open steady to 0.200 cent higher and feeder cattle futures were called up 0.200 to 0.300 cent, analysts said.

Active fed cattle traded at $72 per cwt Tuesday and the discount of futures to cash was seen as supportive for live futures. Cash cattle markets were stronger than expected and packers bought cattle this week sooner than anticipated which shows strong demand, they said.
Continued rising choice boxed beef values were also cited for support, they said.
Lightweight choice boxed beef has rising almost $3.50 per cwt in the past week and currently stands at $117.60 per cwt, the highest price level since Aug 19, 1993.

Feeders were again seen higher after posting new contract highs in most months Tuesday. The latest CME index was at an 11-month high and active fed cattle movement and expected increased feed supplies should keep the undertone strong, analysts said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was up $0.41 to $64.42 per cwt, the highest level since December 27, 1995.
